metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.30) after a sharp drop, model tends to overshoot recovery — cap upward correction at +1.5% of recent 7-day average.
- After a price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward — apply a “mean reversion buffer” to prevent excessive sell-off in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is persistently negative (avg < -0.40) over last 7 days, model underestimates downside risk — add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model exhibits “late horizon lag” — true values often diverge from forecast only after day 15–20 — apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility beyond day 15.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.20–0.30), model tends to overpredict volatility — reduce forecast variance by 20–30% in such regimes.
